about: known-answer vectors for design sections 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 (authenticated box, revised 2026-11-27), 3.5, 3.6, 3.8, 3.8a (the grant) and 3.9, generated by Go (internal/clientproto); regenerate with UPDATE_VECTORS=1

bind.bind: mac[0:16], base64url without padding, sent as the request's bind

cases.name: reference
another sign key
cases.note: a relay that substitutes the sign key gets a different bind and check

cases.name: another box key
cases.note: a relay that substitutes the box key gets a different bind and check

cases.name: another link key
cases.note: without the link key nothing matches

cases.name: keys swapped
cases.note: the order of the two keys is part of the text

cases.name: all-zero keys

bind.check: decimal4( uint16_be(mac[16:18]) mod 10000 ), zero padded; both ends compute it locally and the relay's own check number is never compared
bind.k_bind: sha256("codeaf/link-bind/v1\n" || link_key) where link_key is the 16 raw bytes behind the token's 22 characters
bind.mac: HMAC-SHA256(k_bind, "client\n" || sign_pub || box_pub), the two keys as raw 32-byte values

call.about: the queued call (design 3.5): outer body {number, at, method, target, sealed} signed with codeaf-req-v1; sealed is the plaintext below anonymously sealed to ONE computer's executor box key (nacl SealAnonymous: ephemeral x25519 key, nonce = blake2b-24(eph_pub || computer_pub), box).

cases.name: ok, agents.create
ok, agents.send
ok, asks.answer
ok, agents.stop
expired, a create one millisecond past not_after
bad_call, outer target changed in transit
bad_call, outer number changed
bad_call, outer method changed
bad_call, sealed body copied into another phone's envelope
bad_call, a ciphertext byte flipped
bad_call, a life longer than a day

call.computer_rules: after opening: refuse (bad_call) unless client == the phone whose queue the entry came from, target == this computer, number, at, method and target equal the outer signed body, number > 0, not_after > at and not_after - at <= 86400000; then, if now > not_after the call is expired, never run. not_after is at + 3600000 for agents.create and at + 86400000 for every other method.

params.agents.create: {"client_id": "<uuid>"}: nothing else. The same client_id from the same phone is the same chat, so a retry under another number maps to the chat the first one made. The chat is started on the computer in `target`, in its default folder, with its default model; the first message follows as agents.send.
params.agents.send: {"id": "<chat id>", "text": "...", "client_id": "<uuid>"}: client_id is echoed on the person's entry, so the phone finds its own message again.
params.asks.answer: {"agent": "<chat id>", "id": "<ask id>", "option": "<option>", "text": "..."}: option and text may be empty strings but not both.

call.plaintext: JSON object with exactly the keys v (1), client, number, at, not_after, target, method, params, face_id, in this order; params is the method's own JSON object
call.reproduce: a case with ephemeral_seed_hex is reproducible: sealed_b64 is SealAnonymous(plaintext_json, executor_box_pub_hex) with that 32-byte ephemeral private key; a case without one was changed after sealing

valid, a name with non-ASCII letters
invalid, name changed after signing
invalid, at changed after signing
invalid, box_pub replaced after signing (what a substituting relay would do)
invalid, writer is not the certificate's device

invalid, signed by a device key that is not the certificate's
invalid, signature is the non-canonical S+L twin

card.label: codeaf-card-v1\n
card.verify: cert verifies under the identity key (hex signature over "codeaf/device-cert/v1\n" + the cert JSON with sig empty); cert.device is the signing key; writer == dev_ + hex(sha256(cert device key)[:16]); the card signature verifies under that device key, strictly (a signature whose S is not below the group order is refused); name is 1 to 32 runes with no control characters; v == 1

card_slot.about: a card travels in slot card.<writer> sealed ANONYMOUSLY to the phone box key (nacl SealAnonymous: ephemeral x25519 key, nonce = blake2b-24(eph_pub || phone_pub), box). The phone has no key for the computer yet; the card's own signature chain authenticates it.
card_slot.expect: opens to card_json, then Card verification under identity_pub_hex succeeds

cases.name: valid
valid, lists written in another order (same signed text)
valid, version 2
valid, empty lists (encoded as arrays, never null)
invalid, a method added after signing
invalid, device is not the hash of sign_pub
invalid, verified under another identity key

enrollment.label: codeaf-enroll-v1\n
enrollment.sign_text:
label + device + 
 + hex(sign_pub) + 
 + hex(box_pub) + 
 + join(sorted(methods),",") + 
 + join(sorted(reads),",") + 
 + decimal(ver)
enrollment.sort_order: byte order of the names (names are ASCII: A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -)

grant.about: the grant the approving computer hands the phone (design 5.1 step 4.3, 3.8a): sealed under a key derived from the link key, so a relay that never sees the link key cannot read, forge or swap it. It travels in the link request's grant field as base64url without padding.

cases.name: accepted, the phone's own request
refused, the grant answers another request code
refused, the grant is for another phone
does not open, sealed by a relay under its own key
does not open, a ciphertext byte flipped
does not open, a nonce byte flipped
does not open, truncated
does not open, the phone's link key is another one

grant.k_grant: sha256("codeaf/phone-grant/v1\n" || link_key), link_key the 16 raw bytes behind the token's 22 characters
grant.phone_rules: after opening: refuse unless device == the phone's own device id, code == the code the relay gave this request, cert.device is the phone's own sign key and the cert verifies under identity_pub, relay is not empty and at least one card verifies under identity_pub (cards that fail are dropped); keep nothing until every check passes. The phone stores relay as the address to use; it should refuse a grant whose relay names another host than the address it made the request at unless it was set up from a setup link that names it.
grant.plaintext: JSON object with exactly the keys v, device, code, cert, identity_pub, relay, executors; v must be 2; identity_pub is standard padded base64 of the 32-byte identity PUBLIC key; cert is the phone's own device certificate; executors holds 1 to 4 cards; unknown keys or trailing data are refused. It never contains a seed, a dedup secret or a cell key.
grant.seal: sealed = nonce(24) || nacl secretbox(plaintext, nonce, k_grant) (xsalsa20 + poly1305), a fresh random nonce per grant

outcomes.about: the outcome slot (design 3.6): a computer publishes one outcome for EVERY queued call it acknowledges, the last 32 in the slot outcomes.<writer>, oldest first. Statuses: done, refused, expired. Reasons: not_holder, needs_face_id, expired, method_denied, bad_target, bad_call (a call that did not open, did not match its outer body or carried params the method does not take). A transient failure publishes nothing: the call stays queued and is tried again.
outcomes.opens_with: the slot box of design 3.4: executor_box_pub_hex below, phone_box_priv_hex 0x12 x 32

signing: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, deterministic); identity seed is 32 bytes of 0x01, the phone's sign seed 32 bytes of 0x02, box_pub 32 bytes of 0x03; JSON byte fields are standard padded base64

slot_box.about: every slot except the card is nonce(24) || nacl box (curve25519 + xsalsa20 + poly1305) between the computer's executor key and the phone's box key, so only those two can compute the shared key. There is no certificate and no signature in a slot (design 3.4, revised 2026-11-27 after the Hermes gate). The phone gets the executor public key ONLY from that computer's verified card.

cases.name: accepted, first slot from this computer
accepted, newer than the last accepted
refused, at equals the last accepted (replay)
refused, at below the last accepted (rollback)
refused, served under another slot name
refused, fetched for another phone
refused, relay says another writer
does not open, wrong executor key
does not open, a ciphertext byte flipped
does not open, a nonce byte flipped
does not open, truncated
does not open, forged by a relay under its own key

slot_box.open: box.Open(sealed[24:], nonce = sealed[:24], executor_box_pub (from the card), phone_box_priv)
slot_box.phone_rules: after opening: refuse unless slot == the name it was fetched as, client == the phone's own device id, executor == the slot's writer (the relay's writer field and the name suffix), and at > the last accepted at for that slot name; ver is recorded and never refused on in v1
slot_box.plaintext: JSON object with exactly the keys v, slot, client, executor, at, ver, payload; payload is standard padded base64 of the entries (or outcomes) JSON array; v must be 1; unknown keys or trailing data are refused
slot_box.seal: sealed = nonce || box.Seal(plaintext, nonce, phone_box_pub, executor_box_priv), a fresh random 24-byte nonce per slot
